agree.reason: The speaker's honesty as a long-time Alder Road neighbour who concedes the traffic cost will win some respect, but the traffic-focused commissioners get no reason to think the C-to-D drop is small, so many objectors will stay unmoved.

honest.reason: Every figure comes from the brief and is stated at its proper strength; "about one in six" (64/412) and "already paved" are fair readings, and the speech claims the homes are enough for one in six households, not that waiting-list households will get them.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the one-in-six share of the waiting list and the eight extra parking spaces, but it never puts the 310 trips in a smaller form, such as per household or per rush hour, and it does little else with the numbers.

right_comparison.reason: It hints at the status quo (an empty lot and a three-year wait) but never says outright that if the project is rejected the shortfall stays and the wait goes on.

qualification.reason: The speech makes no forecast that depends on an uncertain outcome, so it doesn't need a hedge or condition.

objections.reason: It takes on traffic directly as a stated trade and settles parking with the 72 spaces, but it leaves the C-to-D drop unsoftened, with no context or mitigation for the commissioners who weigh it most.

fit.reason: It is a spoken public comment of about 380 words, which fits comfortably in three minutes, with a proper opening, a direct ask and a close.
